description: Study tag. Constant.

Counterbalance version drawn at random per session. Defines trial order, which classmate receives the higher-rung content, which food item is asked first, and the practice layout. See OMIT3_counterbalance_spec.md.
Children Helping Science response id, from the response_uuid URL parameter. The join key back to the CHS record (demographics, webcam, exit survey).
Set when the protocol loads.
Set when the rows are built at debrief.
Which side Quinn (the stated best friend) appeared on in the practice block. Counterbalanced.
Practice response-training item ("Who is Sam's best friend?"). 1 = correct on the FIRST attempt. Wrong answers are corrected and re-asked, so 0 means the child needed the correction.
Attempts taken on that item. Capped at 3.
Practice manipulation check. 1 = chose the best friend for the single-straw juice box. Tests that children read a single-portion item as intimate; expected 1. This is the check for the ice cream DV.
Practice comparison item. 1 = chose the best friend for the divisible cookies. No directional prediction; parallels the candy DV.
Serial position of this trial within the session. Trial order follows a Williams square balanced for first-order carryover.
Which contents were pitted against each other. SH = sad vs happy; SF = sad vs fact; HF = happy vs fact; PF = personal preference vs fact.
The character who discloses. Fixed per trial.
Classmate shown on the left.
Classmate shown on the right.
The higher-rung content in this trial, i.e. the one predicted to signal greater closeness.
The lower-rung content.
Which classmate was told the higher-rung content (1 = left / 2 = right). Counterbalanced.
Name of the classmate told the higher-rung content. Redundant with hi_told_to; kept for readability.
Which of the two mirrored narration sets played (follows hi_told_to).
Which food item was asked first. Constant within child; counterbalanced across versions.
SH trial only. Which emotion the protagonist felt first. Blank elsewhere.
SH trial only. Where the sad episode occurred; the happy episode takes the other scene. Blank elsewhere.
PF trial only. Which animal was the protagonist's favourite. Blank elsewhere.
Yes/no comprehension check: was classmate 1 told the higher-rung content? 1 = correct on the FIRST attempt. Wrong answers are corrected and re-asked.
Same for classmate 2.
Yes/no comprehension check for the lower-rung content and classmate 1.
Same for classmate 2.
1 if all four checks in this trial were correct first time. Convenience column for exclusion rules; the rule itself must be pre-registered.
PRIMARY DV. 1 = chose the classmate told the HIGHER-rung content as the better friend. Note this is coded relative to the rung, not to a fixed side or character.
Name of the classmate chosen. Useful for checking the coding above.
Time from the scene becoming clickable to the click.
Caregiver-typed answer to "Why do you think that?", asked after the better-friend judgment only. Empty when the probe is disabled or left blank.
SECONDARY DV. 1 = chose the classmate told the higher-rung content for the single ice cream cone (the item requiring physical intimacy).
Response time for the ice cream item.
SECONDARY DV. 1 = chose the classmate told the higher-rung content for the partitionable candy (the divisible comparison item).
Response time for the candy item.
